Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verses 1–2:

(p-188) Surat al-Ankabut (The Spider) is Meccan, and its verses number sixty-nine.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Alif. Lam. Mim.﴾ The discussion of it has already passed. The occurrence of the interrogative after it is evidence that it stands by itself, or that what is implied with it is independent.

﴿Do people think﴾ (ahasiba al-nas): al-husban (reckoning, thinking) is among the verbs that relate to the contents of sentences, to indicate the manner of their establishment. For this reason it requires two objects that are interdependent, or what takes their place, as in His saying: ﴿that they will be left alone because they say, "We believe," and they will not be tested﴾. Its meaning is: "Do they reckon that their being left is without being tested for their saying 'We believe'?" So the leaving (al-tark) is its first object, and "without being tested" completes it, and their saying "We believe" is the second, as in your saying: "I reckoned his striking to be for discipline." Or the meaning is: "Do they reckon themselves left, untested, for their saying 'We believe'?" Rather, Allah tests them with the hardships of obligations, such as emigration, striving, abandoning desires, the duties of acts of worship, and various kinds of calamities in their persons and property, so that the sincere is distinguished from the hypocrite, and the steadfast in religion from the wavering in it, and so that by patience through them they attain lofty ranks. For mere faith, even if it is sincere, requires nothing beyond deliverance from eternal punishment.

It is narrated that it was revealed concerning some of the Companions who became distressed by the harm of the polytheists. It was also said that it was revealed concerning ʿAmmar, who was tortured for the sake of Allah the Exalted. It was also said that it was revealed concerning Mihja', the freed slave of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, whom ʿAmir ibn al-Hadrami struck with an arrow on the day of Badr, killing him, and his parents and his wife grieved over him.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 3–4:

﴿And We certainly tested those before them﴾ is connected either to (a-ḥasiba, "Do people think") or to (lā yuftanūn, "they will not be tested"). The meaning is that this is an ancient practice (sunnah qadīmah) prevailing among all nations, so it should not be expected that its opposite occurs. ﴿So Allah will surely know those who are truthful, and He will surely know the liars﴾. His knowledge is connected to the testing in a manner of occurrence (ta‘alluqan ḥāliyyan), by which those who were truthful in faith are distinguished from those who lied concerning it, and their reward and punishment are made dependent upon that. It has been said that the meaning is "He will surely distinguish" or "He will surely requite." It was also read as «and He will surely make known» (wa-la-yu‘limanna), from the causative (al-i‘lam), meaning: Allah will surely make them known to people, or will mark them with a mark by which they will be recognized on the Day of Resurrection, like the whiteness and blackness of faces.

﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think﴾ — that is, disbelief and sins, since "deeds" (‘amal) encompasses the actions of the hearts and the limbs — ﴿that they will outstrip Us?﴾ That is, that they will escape Us, so that We will not be able to requite them for their wrongdoing. This clause (an yasbiqūnā) occupies the place of the two objects of (ḥasiba), since it contains a predicate and a subject. It is also permissible that (ḥasiba) be taken in the sense of (qadara, "to determine"), or that (am) be disjunctive (munqaṭi‘ah), with the turning away (al-iḍrāb) in it because this supposition has been nullified from the first. For this reason He follows it with His saying: ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, that is, wretched is what they judge, or a judgment they make: their judgment is this. Thus the object of the dispraise has been omitted.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 5:

﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah﴾ (i.e., in Paradise). It is also said that what is meant by "the meeting with Allah" is attaining His reward, or the final outcome after death (p-189)

and resurrection, reckoning and recompense. This is an analogy for his state with the state of a servant who comes before his master after a long time, while the master has been informed of his conduct: the master will either meet him with joy, for what he approved of his deeds, or with displeasure, for what he disapproved of in them. ﴿Then indeed the term of Allah﴾, meaning the appointed time for that meeting, ﴿is surely coming﴾, meaning it is arriving. And when the time of the meeting is coming, the meeting is bound to happen without doubt, so let him hasten to do what will fulfil his hope and make his expectation true, or what will earn him nearness and approval. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing﴾ of the words of the servants, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of their beliefs and their deeds.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verses 6–7:

﴿And whoever strives﴾ (jahada) his soul by patiently bearing the hardship of obedience and by restraining it from desires. ﴿Then he strives only for his own soul﴾, because its benefit returns to it. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Free of need from the worlds﴾, so He has no need for their obedience. Rather, He imposed duties upon His servants out of mercy towards them and in consideration of their welfare.

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely remove from them their misdeeds﴾: this means disbelief is removed by faith, and sins are removed by the acts of obedience that follow them. ﴿And We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾, i.e., We will reward them for their deeds with the best of rewards.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verses 8–9:

﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents.﴾ [That is], by giving them an act that is good, or as though it were in itself good because of its excellence. "Waṣṣā" (enjoined) takes the course of a command in meaning and in its usage. It is said that it has the sense of "qāla" (said), i.e., "And We said to him: Be good to your parents" (ḥusnan). It is also said that "ḥusnan" is in the accusative governed by a hidden verb, on the assumption of an explanatory "qawl" (saying) for the enjoining, i.e., "We said, first of them" or "Act towards them with ḥusnan (goodness)." This is more in harmony with what follows, and on this reading it is good to pause at "bi-wālidayhi" (to his parents). It has also been read as "ḥasanan" and "iḥsānan."

﴿And if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge﴾ regarding His divinity. He expressed its negation by the negation of knowledge of it, indicating that what cannot be known to be correct may not be followed, even if its falsehood is not known, let alone what is known to be false.

﴿Then do not obey them﴾ in that matter, for there is no obedience to a creature in disobedience to the Creator. The word "qawl" (saying) must be understood as implied, if it was not implied before.

﴿To Me is your return﴾: the return of those among you who believed, and of those who associated partners, and of those who were dutiful to their parents, and of those who were undutiful.

﴿So I will inform you of what you used to do﴾, by recompensing you for it. The verse was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and his mother Hamnah, for when she heard of his conversion she swore that she would not move from the sun, nor eat nor drink until he apostatized. She remained three days in this state. The same applies to the verses in Luqman and al-Ahqaf.

﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds – We will surely admit them among the righteous﴾ into their company. Perfection in righteousness is the highest rank of the believers and the wish of God's prophets and messengers. Or [it means] "in their entrance," which is Paradise.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 10–11:

﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah﴾, by the disbelievers torturing them for their faith. ﴿He considers the trial of people﴾ what befalls him of their harm, in turning him away from faith, ﴿as the punishment of Allah﴾ in turning him away from disbelief. ﴿And if there comes victory from your Lord﴾, meaning conquest and spoils, ﴿they will surely say, "Indeed, we were with you"﴾ in the religion, so give us a share in it. What is meant is the hypocrites, or a people whose faith was weak, so they apostatized because of the harm of the polytheists. The first interpretation is supported by ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of what is in the breasts of the worlds?﴾, that is, of sincerity and hypocrisy.

﴿And Allah will surely make known those who believe﴾ with their hearts, ﴿and He will surely make known the hypocrites﴾, so that He may recompense both groups.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verses 12–13:

﴿And those who disbelieved said to those who believed: "Follow our way"﴾ — the way that we tread in our religion. ﴿"And let us bear your sins"﴾ — if that is a sin, or if there is resurrection and reckoning. They ordered themselves to bear [the sins] in a manner that follows their command to follow [them], as an exaggeration in making the bearing of burdens conditional upon following, and in promising the lightening of their burdens if they follow. This is in order to encourage them to it. And in this regard He answered them and denied them with His saying: ﴿"And they are not in the least bearers of their sins. Indeed, they are liars."﴾ The first "min" (from) is for explanation (tabyin), and the second is superfluous (zaidah), and the estimate is: "They are not bearers of anything of their sins."

﴿"And they will surely bear their burdens"﴾ — the burdens of what their own selves committed. ﴿"And burdens along with their burdens"﴾ — and other burdens along with them, for what they caused by misguidance and by driving [others] to acts of disobedience, without the burdens of those who followed them being diminished in any way. ﴿"And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection"﴾ — a questioning of rebuke and reproach. ﴿"About what they used to fabricate"﴾ — of the falsehoods with which they misled.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verses 14–15:

﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years﴾ after the commissioning (al-mab'ath), for it is narrated that he was commissioned at the age of forty, that he called his people for nine hundred and fifty years, and that he lived sixty years after the flood. Perhaps the choice of this expression is to indicate the completeness of the number, since nine hundred and fifty may be used for what approximates it, and because mentioning the thousand conveys to the hearer an imagination of the length of the period. The purpose of the story is to console the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and to strengthen him in what he endures from the disbelievers. The difference between the two specifications (al-mumayyizayn) is for the sake of avoiding the ugliness of repetition. ﴿Then the flood seized them﴾ the flood of water, and it is called tufan (flood) because of its overflowing in abundance, whether a torrent, or darkness, or the like.

﴿while they were wrongdoers﴾ through disbelief.

﴿So We saved him﴾ i.e., Noah, peace be upon him. ﴿and the people of the ark﴾ and whoever rode with him of his children and followers, and they were eighty. It is said seventy-eight, and it is said ten, half of them males and half females. ﴿And We made it﴾ i.e., the ark, or the event.

﴿a sign for the worlds﴾ who take warning and draw lessons from it.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 16–17:

﴿And Abraham﴾: it is conjoined to (Noah) [i.e., "and We sent Abraham" follows the sense of "Noah"], or it is put in the accusative by supposing "remember" (udhkur) implied. It is also read in the nominative, on the reckoning of "and among the messengers, Abraham." ﴿When he said to his people: Worship Allah﴾: it is an adverbial clause of time governed by "We sent," meaning: We sent him when his intellect was complete and his reflection was perfected, such that he recognized the truth and commanded the people to it. Or it is a substitution from it (a substitution of inclusion), if it is taken as governed by "remember." ﴿And fear Him. That is better for you﴾ than what you are upon. ﴿If you but knew﴾ good and evil, and could distinguish what is better from what is worse; or, you were looking at matters with the gaze of knowledge and not the gaze of ignorance.

﴿You only worship, besides Allah, idols, and you create a lie﴾: you lie in naming them gods and in claiming that they intercede for you with Allah the Exalted; or, you make them and carve them for falsehood. This is an argument for the vileness of what they are upon, in that it is falsehood and nullity. It is also read "takhluqun" (from khalaqa, for intensification) and "tukhalliqun" (from takhalloqa, for effort). "Ifkan" is either a verbal noun like "al-kadhib" (the lie), or an adjective in the sense of "a creation possessing falsehood." ﴿Indeed those whom you worship besides Allah do not possess for you any provision﴾: a second proof of the vileness of that, in that it is of no benefit at all. "Rizqan" may be the verbal noun, in the sense that they are not able to provide for you; or it may mean the thing provided, and its indefiniteness is for generality. ﴿So seek provision from Allah﴾, all of it, for He is its owner. ﴿And worship Him and give thanks to Him﴾, seeking your aims through His worship and binding the blessings that surround you through thanking Him, or preparing yourselves to meet Him through these two. ﴿To Him you will be returned.﴾ It is also read with a fatha on the ta'.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verses 18–19:

﴿And if you deny﴾, and if you deny me. ﴿Then truly nations before you denied﴾, before me, of the messengers. ﴿Their denial did not harm them﴾, rather it harmed only themselves, since it brought upon them the punishment that befell them. So too is your denial. ﴿And upon the Messenger is only the clear delivery﴾, which removes doubt by its means. It is not incumbent upon him to be believed and not denied. Thus this verse and what follows are part of the story of Ibrahim, up to His saying ﴿So there was not the answer of his people﴾. It is possible that they are an i'tiraḍ (interjected clause) mentioning the affair of the Prophet ﷺ and Quraysh, the demolition of their creed, and the threat for their evil conduct. It is placed between the two ends of his story, in that its purpose is to console the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and to relieve him, by showing that his father, the Friend of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon them both), was afflicted with something similar to what he was afflicted with, namely the polytheism and denial of his people. His situation among them is likened to the situation of Ibrahim among his people.

﴿Have they not seen how Allah originates creation﴾, from material and from other than material. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr read it with the ta' (تاء), on the presumption of an implied "say" (القول). It is also read as "yabda'" (يَبْدَأُ). ﴿Then He repeats it﴾: this is a statement about the resurrection after death, coordinated with (أوَلَمْ يَرَوْا) and not with (يُبْدِئُ), since the seeing does not fall upon it. It is also permissible to interpret the repetition as Allah producing each year the like of what was in the previous year of plants, fruits and the like, and then it is coordinated with (يُبْدِئُ). ﴿Indeed that﴾: the demonstrative refers to the repetition, or to what was mentioned of the two matters. ﴿Is easy for Allah﴾, since He does not depend in His action upon anything.

﴿So each﴾ of those mentioned. ﴿We seized for his sin﴾ — We punished him for his sin. ﴿Among them is one upon whom We sent a violent wind with pebbles﴾ — a fierce wind in which there were pebbles; or an angel who pelted them with them, like the people of Lot. ﴿And among them is one who was seized by the Blast﴾ — like Madyan and Thamud. ﴿And among them is one whom We caused the earth to swallow﴾ — like Qarun. ﴿And among them is one whom We drowned﴾ — like the people of Noah, and Pharaoh and his people. ﴿And Allah would not have wronged them﴾ — that He would deal with them in the manner of a wrongdoer, punishing them without a crime, since that is not His custom, Mighty and Majestic is He. ﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾ — by exposing themselves to punishment.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 41:

﴿The parable of those who take protectors other than Allah﴾ — in what they have taken as a support and a reliance.

﴿is like the parable of the spider, which takes a house﴾ — in what it weaves, in weakness and fragility. Rather, that [house] is weaker, for this [house] has a certain reality and some benefit. Or, their parable in relation to the One God is like its parable in relation to a man who built a house of stone and gypsum. The spider (al-'ankabut) applies to the singular and the plural, the masculine and the feminine, and its "ta'" is like the "ta'" in ṭāghūt. It is pluralized as 'anākīb, 'anākib, 'ukāb, 'ikbah and a'kub.

﴿And indeed the frailest of houses is the house of the spider﴾ — there is no house that is weaker, or that offers less protection from heat and cold, than it.

﴿if only they knew﴾ — that is, if they would return to knowledge, they would know that this is their parable and that their religion is weaker than that. It is also possible that what is meant by "the house of the spider" is their religion; he called it that to make the comparison concrete, so the meaning is: the frailest of what is relied upon in religion is their religion.

﴿Indeed, Allah knows what they call upon besides Him of anything.﴾ This is on the supposition of an elided verb of saying, meaning: Say to the disbelievers, "Indeed, Allah knows..." The two Basran readers (Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub) read ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ with a *ya* (the third-person form), taking it as continuing what precedes it. The word ﴿ما﴾ may be interrogative (*istifhamiyya*), in the accusative governed by ﴿تَدْعُونَ﴾ ("you call upon"), while ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ is suspended (*mu'allaqa*, meaning the verb of knowing is held back from governing its object because of the interrogative). In that case ﴿مِن﴾ is explanatory (*lil-tabyin*). Alternatively, ﴿ما﴾ may be negative, with ﴿مِن﴾ being superfluous (*mazida*) and ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ the object of ﴿تَدْعُونَ﴾. Or ﴿ما﴾ may be a verbal-masdar particle (*masdariyya*), with ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ being a masdar, or a relative pronoun (*mawsula*), the object of ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾, with the object of ﴿تَدْعُونَ﴾ being its omitted returning pronoun. The statement, on the first two readings, is a rebuke of them (*tajhil*) and a confirmation of the parable; on the last two readings, it is a threat (*wa'id*) against them.

﴿And He is the Almighty, the Wise.﴾ This is a reason (*ta'lil*) for both meanings. For indeed, it is from the extreme of foolishness to associate with the One who has such a status that which is not counted as anything at all. And a lifeless thing, in comparison to the All-Powerful, the Irresistible over every thing, who is supremely perfect in knowledge and in the mastery of action, is like nothing. And the One who has this attribute is able to recompense them.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verses 43–44:

﴿And these examples – We set them forth for the people﴾, meaning this parable and its like, ﴿and none understands them except the knowledgeable﴾ – as a means of bringing near what is far from their understanding. ﴿And none understands them﴾ – that is, does not comprehend their beauty and benefit – ﴿except the knowledgeable﴾, those who reflect upon things as they ought to be reflected upon.

And from him (ﷺ) that he recited this verse, then said: "The knowledgeable one is he who understands from Allah and so acts in His obedience and avoids His displeasure."

﴿Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth﴾ – in truth, not intending by it falsehood; for the primary purpose of their creation is to convey good and to indicate His essence and attributes, as He pointed out with His words: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers﴾, because they are the ones who benefit from it.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 45:

﴿Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book﴾ seeking nearness to God Most High by reciting it, preserving its words, and seeking to uncover its meanings, for the reflective reader may come to see through repetition what did not become clear to him when it first struck his hearing. ﴿And establish the prayer. Indeed, the prayer forbids immorality and wrongdoing﴾ in that it is a cause of desisting from sins while one is occupied with it and at other times, insofar as it reminds one of God and produces in the soul fear of Him.

It is related that "a young man from the Ansar used to pray with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) the prayers, and he would not leave any of the abominations without committing it. He was described to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), peace be upon him, and he said: 'Indeed, his prayer will restrain him.' So he did not delay before repenting."

﴿And the remembrance of God is greater﴾ and the prayer is greater than the rest of the acts of obedience. He expressed it by this [remembrance] to indicate the reason, namely that its including the remembrance of Him is the principal factor in its being preferred over good deeds and in its forbidding evil deeds. Or [the meaning is]: and the remembrance of God of you with His mercy is greater than your remembrance of Him with your obedience. ﴿And God knows what you do﴾ of it and of the rest of the acts of obedience, so He will reward you for it in the best of recompense.

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verses 46–47:**

﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in the best manner﴾: except with the best way, such as countering harshness with gentleness, anger with restraint, and contention with sincere advice. It has been said that it is abrogated (*mansukh*, meaning abrogated by *naskh*, the doctrine of abrogation) by the verse of the sword, since there is no argument more severe than that. Its response is that it is the last resort of remedies. It has also been said that what is meant are those of them who have a covenant (*dhu al-ʿahd*).

﴿Except those of them who have done wrong﴾ through excessive aggression and obstinacy, or by ascribing offspring (to God), and their saying ﴿The hand of God is chained﴾, or by breaking the covenant and refusing the *jizya* (the poll tax levied on non-Muslim subjects).

﴿And say: We believe in what has been sent down to us and what has been sent down to you﴾: this is from arguing in the best manner.

It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Do not believe the People of the Book, nor disbelieve them, but say: We believe in God and His books and His messengers. If they say something false, do not believe them, and if they say something true, do not disbelieve them."

﴿Our God and your God is One, and to Him we are submitting﴾: obedient to Him alone. In this there is an allusion to their taking their rabbis and monks as lords besides God.

﴿And thus﴾: and like that sending down. ﴿We have sent down to you the Book﴾: as a revelation confirming the other divine books. This is a confirmation of His saying: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book believe in it﴾. They are ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and his like, or those among the People of the Book who preceded the time of the Messenger (ﷺ).

﴿And among these﴾: and among the Arabs, or the people of Makkah, or those from the People of the Two Books in the time of the Messenger. ﴿Are those who believe in it﴾: in the Qur'an. ﴿And none reject Our signs﴾: despite their clarity and the establishment of proof against them. ﴿Except the disbelievers﴾: except those who plunge deeply into disbelief, for their firm conviction in it prevents them from reflecting on what would show them its truth, since it is a miracle in relation to the Messenger (ﷺ), as he indicated by his saying:

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verses 48–49:

﴿You did not recite any scripture before it, nor did you write one with your right hand﴾. For the appearance of this Book, comprehensive of the various kinds of noble sciences (p-197) upon an unlettered man who was not known for reading or learning, is a violation of the customary order. The mention of the "right hand" is an added emphasis in depicting the negated act and a negation of metaphorical usage in the attribution. ﴿Otherwise the falsifiers would have had cause for doubt﴾. That is, had you been one who writes and reads, they would have said, "Perhaps he learned it or picked it up from the books of the earlier, ancient peoples." He called them "falsifiers" (mubtilun) because of their disbelief, or because of their doubt arising from the absence of even one of the many aspects of inimitability (i'jaz). It has also been said that "the People of the Book would have doubted" because they found your description contrary to what is in their books; in that case their falsification is considered in relation to the actual reality, not the hypothetical.

﴿Rather, it is﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾, who memorize it; no one can alter it.

﴿And none deny Our signs except the wrongdoers﴾, those who go to extremes in wrongdoing through obstinacy after the clarity of the proofs of its inimitability, to the point that they do not regard them at all.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 50–51:

(And they say, "Why has not a sign been sent down upon him from his Lord?") like the she-camel of Salih, the staff of Musa, and the table of Isa. Nafi', Ibn Amir, the two Basrans (Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub), and Hafs read (ayat) in the plural form (ayat, "signs").

﴿Say, "Indeed, the signs are with Allah. He sends them down as He wills. I do not possess them, so I will bring you what you propose."﴾

﴿And I am only a clear warner﴾: it is not my task except to warn and to make it clear by means of the signs that I have been given.

﴿Is it not sufficient for them﴾ as a sign that suffices in place of what they have proposed? ﴿That We have sent down to you the Book, which is recited to them﴾: its recitation continues upon them, unified in it, so it remains with them as a lasting sign that does not perish, unlike the other signs. Or, "which is recited to them" means the Jews, by verifying what is in their hands of your description and the description of your religion. ﴿Indeed, in that﴾ Book, which is a continuing sign and a manifest proof, ﴿is surely a mercy﴾, a great blessing, ﴿and a reminder for a people who believe﴾, a reminder for whoever is inclined toward faith, without obstinacy.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 54–55:

﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed Hell encompasses the disbelievers﴾ It will encompass them on the Day the punishment comes upon them; or it is already, as it were, encompassing them now, because of the disbelief and the sins that necessitate it, which encompass them. ﴿O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is spacious, so worship only Me.﴾ That is: if worship is not made easy for you in a land, and it is not possible for you to openly practise your religion, then emigrate (hijrah) to wherever it is feasible for you to do so. Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verses 58–59:

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely settle them﴾ (*lanunzilannahum*, "We will surely cause them to dwell"). ﴿in lofty chambers (ghurafan) of Paradise﴾ (*ʿalāliy*, "high, elevated"), beneath which rivers flow, ﴿abiding therein forever. Excellent is the reward of the doers﴾. It is also read *fa-niʿma* (with the fāʾ). The specified object of praise (*al-makhsūs bil-madh*, the noun that the verb of praise is made to govern) is omitted, and what precedes it indicates it.

The accusative case of *ghurafan* (*intiṣāb*, the accusative) is then either because the verb is treated as *lanunzilannahum*, or by omitting the preposition (*naz' al-khāfid*), or by treating the temporal adverbial (*al-ẓarf al-muʾaqqat*) as if it were the indefinite (*al-mubham*).

The accusative case of *ghurafan* (*intiṣāb*, the accusative) is then either because the verb is treated as *lanunzilannahum*, or by omitting the preposition (*naz' al-khāfid*), or by treating the temporal adverbial (*al-ẓarf al-muʾaqqat*) as if it were the indefinite (*al-mubham*).

﴿Those who were patient﴾ in the face of the harm of the polytheists, and in migrating for the sake of the religion, and in other trials and hardships, ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾, and they rely upon none but God.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verses 60–61:

﴿And how many a creature does not carry its provision﴾. It is unable to carry it because of its weakness, or it does not store it; rather, it wakes up in the morning with no livelihood with it.

﴿God provides for it and for you﴾. Then, despite its weakness and its reliance (on God), and your strength and your striving, it is the same in that none provides for it and for you except God, because the provision of all comes through means, but He alone is the one who causes it. So do not fear for your livelihood through the emigration (hijrah, migration). When they were commanded to emigrate, some of them said, "How can we go to a land where we have no livelihood?" So this was revealed. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing﴾ of your saying this. ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of what is in your hearts.

﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?"﴾ The ones being asked are the people of Makkah (Mecca). ﴿They will surely say, "God."﴾ This is because it has been established in the intellects that contingent beings (mumkinat) must terminate in one being whose existence is necessary (wajib al-wujud). ﴿Then how are they turned away?﴾ They are diverted from His oneness (tawhid) after acknowledging that.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verses 62–63:

﴿Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants, and restricts it for him.﴾ It is possible that the one for whom provision is expanded and the one for whom it is restricted are the same person, on the basis that extending and restricting occur in succession. It is also possible that the pronoun is not placed in the position of "whom He wills," and that its indefiniteness is intended, because "whom He wills" is indefinite.

﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of everything.﴾ He knows their benefits (maṣāliḥ) and their harms (mafāsid).

﴿And if you asked them, "Who sends down water from the sky and thereby gives life to the earth after its death?" they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ Acknowledging that He is the originator of all possible things, both their roots and their branches. Yet they associate with Him some of His creatures, which have no power over any of that.

﴿Say, "All praise is for Allah."﴾ For having protected you from the like of this error, or for your affirmation and the manifestation of your proof. ﴿But most of them do not reason.﴾ So they contradict themselves: they acknowledge that He is the originator of everything besides Himself, and yet they associate with Him an idol. It is also said: they do not understand what you intend by praising God when they make their statement.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 64:

﴿And this worldly life﴾ is an expression of contempt. And how could it not be, when it does not weigh the wing of a gnat before Allah? ﴿is nothing but amusement and play﴾ — except as children are amused and play with it, gathering around it and rejoicing in it for a while, then dispersing exhausted. ﴿And indeed, the Last Abode — that is the [true] life, if they only knew﴾ — it is the abode of true life, because death cannot befall it; or it is in itself life, for emphasis. Al-hayawan (life/living) is a verbal noun used when it is applied to that which possesses life; its root is hayayan, then the second yaa' was changed to waw. It is more eloquent than al-hayah (life) because of the pattern fa'alan, which implies movement and agitation, which are inherent in life; and for this reason it was chosen over it here. ﴿If only they knew﴾ — they would not have preferred over it the worldly life, whose origin is the absence of life, and whose life is a temporary accident, quick to vanish.

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on Surah 29, verses 65–66:**

﴿So when they board the ship﴾ is connected to what is implied by the description of their state, meaning: they are in the condition described, of associating partners with Allah, so when they board the sea. ﴿They call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾, being in the form of one who has made his religion sincere from among the believers, in that they mention none but Allah and invoke none other than Him, knowing that none removes the calamities except Him. ﴿But when He has brought them safely to the land, immediately they associate others with Him﴾: they hastened to return to associating partners with Allah.

﴿So that they may deny what We have given them﴾: the lam in it is the lam of purpose (lam ka'y, "in order that"), meaning they associate partners with Allah so that they may be ungrateful for the blessing of deliverance through their polytheism. ﴿And so that they may enjoy themselves﴾: through their gathering in the worship of idols and their mutual affection over them. Or it is the lam of command (lam al-amr, "let"), in the sense of a threat, and it is supported by the recitation of Ibn Kathir, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Qalun on the authority of Nafi', ﴿wa-liyatamatta'u﴾ with a sukun (silent vowel on the lam). ﴿But they will come to know﴾ the outcome of that when they are punished.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verses 67–68:

﴿Have they not seen﴾ meaning the people of Makkah. ﴿That We have made a sanctuary secure﴾ i.e., We have made their land protected from plunder and aggression, secure (p-200)

for its inhabitants from killing and captivity. ﴿While people are snatched away from around them﴾ they are seized by way of killing and captivity, since the Arabs around it were in raiding and plundering. ﴿Do they then believe in falsehood﴾ after this manifest blessing and others like it, which none can bestow except Allah, do they believe in the idol or the devil? ﴿And are ungrateful for the blessing of Allah﴾ in that they associate others with Him. The placing of the two relative clauses first serves emphasis or exclusivity, by way of intensification.

﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah﴾ by claiming that He has a partner. ﴿Or denies the truth when it has come to him﴾ meaning the Messenger or the Book. The word ﴿lamma﴾ (when) conveys a rebuke against them, in that they did not reflect or consider at all when it came to them, but rushed to denial the moment they heard it. ﴿Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?﴾ This is an affirmation of their dwelling there, like his saying:

"Were you not the best of those who rode the mounts?"

That is: do they not deserve to dwell therein, since they have fabricated this same lie against Allah and denied the truth with this same denial? Or, on account of their audacity, i.e., did they not know that ﴿in Hell there is an abode for the disbelievers﴾, so that they became bold in such audacity?

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 69:

﴿Those who strive in Our cause﴾: in regard to Our right. The word *mujahadah* (striving) is used without restriction so that it includes striving against the outward and inward enemies in all its forms.

﴿We will surely guide them to Our paths﴾: the paths of journeying toward Us and arriving at Our presence. Or it means: We will surely increase them in guidance to the path of good and grant them success in following it, like His saying: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance﴾. In the hadith: "Whoever acts on what he knows, Allah makes him inherit knowledge of what he did not know."

﴿And indeed Allah is with the doers of good﴾: with victory and help.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surah al-'Ankabut, he will have the reward of ten good deeds for each of the believers and the hypocrites."
